landing.heroDesc: Chess, Xiangqi, Ô ăn quan, and plenty of other classics. Invite classmates, coworkers, or family — near or far. No one around? Play against the bot instead.
landing.gamesDesc: Play with a friend, or solo against the bot.
landing.gamesMore: More games are on the way.
landing.howDesc: Play right in your browser — no installs needed.
landing.step1Desc: Pick a game, then tap "Play online" to open a new room.
landing.step2Desc: Send the room code, the link, or let your friend scan the QR code.
landing.step3Desc: Play and chat right in the room. When the match ends, play again or switch games.
landing.faq1Q: Can we play together on two different phones/computers?
landing.faq1A: Yes. Pick a game, tap "Play online" to open a room, then send the code or link to your friend.
landing.faq2Q: Can I play with a friend far away?
landing.faq2A: Yes, as long as you're both online. Join the same room with a code — distance doesn't matter.
landing.faq3Q: Does my friend need to install anything?
landing.faq3A: No. They just open the link in a browser and can play right away — nothing to download.
landing.faq4A: No. Thư Giãn needs no sign-up or login — just open it and play.

settings.title: Me
settings.whatIsSentBody: When enabled, the app only sends anonymous data: which game was played, difficulty, and the win/loss/draw result. No nickname, chat content, or identifying info is ever sent. There's no real collection server behind this yet — the toggle just records your preference for when there is.
settings.feedbackCopied: Copied! Paste it wherever you'd like to send it.
settings.feedbackNote: The app doesn't have a server to receive feedback automatically yet — copy the text and send it through whatever channel you prefer.
settings.troubleshootBody: If an online game disconnects: 1) Check your own network is up. 2) Try "Leave game" and rejoin with the same room code. 3) If your opponent also dropped, wait for them to come back — the game resyncs automatically. 4) Still stuck? Create a new room and share the new code.

points: 3x3 board, two players alternate placing X and O.
Line up 3 of your marks in a row (horizontal, vertical, or diagonal) to win instantly.
If all 9 cells fill up with no winner, it's a draw.
Play against the bot (4 difficulty levels), with a friend on the same device, or online.
15x15 board, two players alternate placing stones.
First to line up 5 stones in a row (horizontal, vertical, or diagonal) wins.
No overline restriction — any run of 5 or more counts (unlike strict tournament rules).
Play against the bot, with a friend on the same device, or online.
12 pits arranged in a ring: 2 big "quan" pits (10 stones each) at either end, and 10 small "dân" pits (5 stones each) split between the two players.

On your turn, pick up all stones from one of your own small pits and sow them one by one into the following pits (always the same direction); if the last stone lands in an occupied pit, pick that pit up too and keep sowing.
If the last stone lands right before an empty pit, you capture whatever is in the pit after that empty one (captures can chain).
The game ends when one side's small pits are all empty; whoever captured more stones wins. (Simplified ruleset: no stone-borrowing "vay quan".)
Standard 8x8 chess with full rules: castling, en passant, and pawn promotion.
Checkmating the opponent's king wins the game.
Draws happen on stalemate, the 50-move rule (no capture or pawn move), or insufficient material to checkmate.
Play against the bot (4 difficulty levels), with a friend on the same device, or online.
Standard Xiangqi: general, advisor, elephant, horse, chariot, cannon, and soldier each move and capture by their own rules.
"Flying general" rule: the two generals may never face each other directly on an open file with nothing in between.
Checkmating the opponent's general, or leaving them with no legal move, wins.
Play against the bot, with a friend on the same device, or online.
9x9 board by default (13x13 or 19x19 can be chosen in "Play options").
Place stones to surround your opponent's: a group with no "liberties" (empty adjacent points) left is captured; a ko rule prevents immediately repeating the same board position.
The game ends once both sides pass in a row — you can choose "mark manually" to decide dead stones yourself instead of letting the game assume everything left on the board is alive.
Scored the Chinese way (stones + surrounded territory); White gets a +7.5 komi bonus, so the game never ends in a draw.
10x10 board; each side hides 5 ships of length 5-4-3-3-2, none overlapping or touching.
Call out coordinates to fire at the opponent's board: a hit lets you fire again, a miss passes the turn.
First to sink all 5 of the opponent's ships wins.
A "Notes" button lets you mark suspicious cells on the opponent's board for free, without using a turn.
Like Battleship, but you hide planes instead of ships — each plane can face 1 of 4 directions (up/right/down/left).
Only hitting the plane's "nose" cell brings it down; hitting any other cell just registers a hit.
Every shot passes the turn, hit or miss — there's no bonus shot.
Board is 10x10 with 3 planes (small) or 15x15 with 5 planes (large); sink all of the opponent's planes to win.
Standard double-six set (28 tiles from 0|0 to 6|6); each player is dealt 7 tiles, the rest form the boneyard.
On your turn, play a tile that matches the pip count on either open end of the line.
If you have no playable tile, draw from the boneyard (how many draws depends on the rule chosen in "Play options"); if the boneyard is empty and you're still stuck, pass.
First to play every tile in hand wins; if both sides get stuck, whoever has fewer pips left in hand wins.
9x9 grid split into 9 3x3 boxes; fill in 1-9 so no row, column, or box repeats a digit.
Difficulty controls how many cells start filled in (Easy gives 42, Expert only 24).
You can turn on "Hints" (fills one cell for you) and pick a mistake limit in "Play options".
Play solo, or invite a friend online for "Race" (first to finish their own copy wins) or "Solve together" (one shared grid).
A 9-column sheet with a number of rows depending on difficulty; each cell holds a number from 1 to 9.

Tap two "adjacent" numbers (next to each other by row/column/diagonal, or wrapping from the end of one row to the start of the next — skipping already-crossed-out cells) that are equal or add up to 10 to cross that pair out.
Solo puzzle: clear the whole sheet to win; stuck with no moves left? Tap "+ Copy numbers" to double what's remaining (limited number of uses).
Against the bot/a friend/online: two players alternate crossing out pairs — whoever has crossed out more pairs when both pass in a row wins.
A sheet scattered with random numbers (15-60 depending on difficulty, or a larger custom sheet size in "Play options").
Tap them in order — 1, then 2, then 3, and so on — until the last one; tapping the wrong number just doesn't count, no penalty.
Solo puzzle: your time is tracked — the faster the better.
Against the bot: a real-time race to see who taps through their own sheet first, each with a separate counter.
